title: test(showcase): separate a silent ablation from a dead instrument in the vitest teardown-race pin
body:
Fixes #11939

## The defect is a conflation, and that is what this closes

The ABLATION leg reported the same red for two different facts:

- **"the race did not open this time"** — a load effect, nothing is wrong;
- **"the mechanism is gone from vitest"** — permanent, upstream, and the moment the whole pin needs re-evaluating.

From the assertion alone they are indistinguishable, which is what the card names as the real gap. Raising `ABLATION_ATTEMPTS` would only have made the symptom rarer while leaving the two states looking alike, so the budget is deliberately **unchanged at 8**.

## What was measured

Every arm serialized under the shared verify lock on this container (4 vCPU / 17 GB), each carrying its own control in the same run:

| condition | reproduced | note |
|---|---|---|
| idle, ablation config | **20/20** | every child exit 1 — positive control |
| idle, this app's config | **0/6** | every child exit 0 — negative control |
| under 4 concurrent vitest processes, measured arm | **3/40** | every child exit 0 and collected |
| those concurrent processes themselves, same windows | **248/1913 (~13%)** | the instrument was demonstrably alive throughout |
| same, each concurrent process on its **own** copy of the fixture root | **3/20** | suppression survives ⇒ not shared-root contention |

Load average held between **2.8 and 3.4 on 4 CPUs with 15 GB free** for the whole load arm — nothing was starved, and reproduction still fell from 100% to ~13%. The card's run 6 had already ruled starvation out from the other side (the file alone under 8 synthetic CPU burners, load ~7, stayed green). **What closes the window is concurrent node processes**, which is exactly what a full-repo `turbo run test` is made of.

Two consequences follow from that number, and both changed the design:

- At ~13% per attempt an 8-attempt budget misses `(1 - 0.13)^8 ≈ 33%` of the time — worse than the 1-in-6 the card observed. No budget that finishes inside a test's lifetime makes a race with an environment-dependent rate reliable. **Route 1 is priced out.**
- The suppressing pressure is *inter-package*: other packages' vitest pools running concurrently. A serial or isolated lane **inside this package cannot isolate the file from it**. **Route 3 is ruled out by measurement**, not by preference.

## What changed

A deterministic **PREMISE probe** that reads the installed vitest's dist chunks and asserts the five links of the mechanism the race walks — mechanising the very instruction the old assertion message gave a human (*"check sendLog/rpcDone in its dist chunks"*). It is static, load-independent, and costs milliseconds:

1. `sendLog` calls the forwarder as a bare statement (nothing holds, awaits or catches the promise);
2. `rpcDone()` awaits a **snapshot** (`Array.from(promises)`) rather than draining until empty;
3. teardown drains and **then** runs its cleanups, in that order;
4. the sweep **rejects** what is still pending;
5. the rejection wording still yields the string the ablation greps for — `TEARDOWN_ERROR` is now **derived** from that template rather than written out a second time, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

The two axes are then graded together:

| premise | race | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| intact | fired | pass |
| intact | silent | **SKIP**, loudly and countably |
| BROKEN | silent | **FAIL**: "the instrument is dead, and this is not the load flake" |
| BROKEN | fired | **FAIL**: "the premise probe is stale, not vitest" |

**The skip cannot become a silent forever-skip.** It is reported as skipped (`Tests 4 passed | 1 skipped (5)` counts it), it prints a greppable `ABLATION-DEGRADED [#11939]` line straight to the worker's stdout, and — the structural half — the premise probe is a **separate, always-run, deterministic assertion**. The leg's floor is never "measured nothing"; it is "measured the mechanism statically".

The probe also carries its **own positive control** (`PREMISE CONTROL`): six minimal mutations of the real chunk text, each modelling the upstream fix that would kill one link. Each case asserts it actually edited something before grading — a no-op edit would let every case pass while measuring nothing — and asserts it breaks **exactly** the marker it names.

## Neither leg is relaxed, and the GUARDED leg still detects the race

Reverse-verified by removing `disableConsoleIntercept: true` from `examples/app-showcase/vitest.config.ts`. Mutation confirmed on disk by anchored grep (`disableConsoleIntercept: true,` count `1 → 0`); restore by `trap` and re-measured. No build or `dist` is involved — vitest reads that config as source when the pin spawns the child.

```
BEFORE anchor_count=1
AFTER  anchor_count=0
MUTATED_LEG_EXIT=1
  x GUARDED: the same fixture exits 0 under this app's real vitest config 2358ms
  AssertionError: 4/4 runs hit the teardown race under the app's own config.
  Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
RESTORED anchor_count=1        -> re-run green: Tests  5 passed (5)
```

## The behaviour change, demonstrated under the condition that used to red it

Running the pin file itself while 4 concurrent vitest processes churn — the arm measured above:

```
PIN_UNDER_LOAD_EXIT=0
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed | 1 skipped (5)
ABLATION-DEGRADED [#11939] the teardown race did not open in 8 attempts, and the premise
probe reads all 5 markers of the mechanism as INTACT in the installed vitest. ...
{"loadWorker":true,"runs":172,"reproduced":31}   <- the race was reproducing on that box
{"loadWorker":true,"runs":173,"reproduced":25}      throughout those same 8 attempts
{"loadWorker":true,"runs":173,"reproduced":19}
{"loadWorker":true,"runs":173,"reproduced":20}
```

Before this change that run was the red. Now it is green, with the leg **skipped rather than passed** and the GUARDED leg still run.

## Out of scope

`#11958` (vitest's worker pool scaling uncapped in 40/41 packages) is plausibly the same pressure this leg is sensitive to and was read before designing, but it has its own card and its own measurement; #11958 is not addressed here.
